title: Local insecticide change explained less than 3% of the gap between expected and observed bird community warming on 3,287 US survey routes in 1992-2012 (route x observer and year effects)
abstract: Question: bird community temperature indices (CTI) on North American Breeding Bird Survey (BBS) routes follow only a small part of the change that the spatial CTI-temperature slope predicts from warming. Did change in agricultural insecticide use remove warm-adapted birds and hide part of this response? Data: 44,050 standard BBS runs on 3,287 contiguous-US routes (1992-2012); USGS EPest county pesticide estimates (neonicotinoids, organophosphates and carbamates, pyrethroids, herbicides) as kg per km2 in a 20 km disc around each route; nClimGrid May-July temperature. Method (plan written before outcomes): run CTI on insecticide intensity and temperature with route x observer and year fixed effects; a gap budget with a 2-degree spatial block bootstrap; pre-trend and lead tests; 12 model variants; 389 per-species Poisson models with meta-regression on species temperature index (STI). Results: the expected CTI trend was 0.207 C per decade and the observed trend 0.034, a gap of 0.173. The insecticide part was -0.0012 C per decade, -0.7% of the gap (95% CI -2.2% to +0.8%). To close the gap, neonicotinoids would need about -1.0 C per kg/km2; the estimate was -0.007 (95% CI -0.019 to +0.005). No neonicotinoid or organophosphate coefficient excluded zero with state clustering. Routes where neonicotinoids later increased already had a relatively decreasing CTI in 1992-2002, so the small estimate is probably not a chemical effect. Species neonicotinoid responses did not depend on STI. Conclusion: local insecticide change is not a material cause of the weak climate tracking. Limitations: year effects remove national-scale effects; EPest values are modelled kg, not toxicity; 2013-2014 used preliminary data because the shared 2013-2017 file was truncated.

A: CTI trend budget for 1992-2012 with 95% 2-degree block-bootstrap intervals: expected trend from the spatial slope, observed trend, gap, insecticide part and herbicide part. B: neonicotinoid part as a fraction of the main gap for 12 model variants (95% CI from model SE).

A: expected and observed CTI trends in terciles of neonicotinoid change; observed trends stay near 0.03 C per decade while warming doubles. B: yearly CTI difference of the middle and high terciles from the low tercile (route x observer demeaned); the difference already moved before the neonicotinoid era.
